title: Changing the world without losing yourself: five lessons from Semmelweis
summary: Using Ignaz Semmelweis, who cut maternal deaths with handwashing but died in an asylum, Garry lays out five lessons for founders pushing new ideas against resistance. The core point: a breakthrough is only half the work; communicating it, persistently and professionally, is the other half.

principles.text: Speak for yourself; data and other people won't carry your message for you.
principles.quote: Don't expect others to speak for you. Certainly the data can't speak for itself. In fact, without you, the data is mute.

principles.text: Practice writing and social media so you can communicate with strangers when it matters.
principles.quote: If you're watching this, you should practice writing and social media. Get into the habit of being able to communicate with strangers on the internet.

principles.text: Don't ragequit; feel the emotion but let the rational part of you make hard decisions.
principles.quote: You do have to make a decision, but when you do, feel the emotions, but be sure it's the rational part of you doing it.

principles.text: The establishment is often wrong; keep saying what you know is right, backed by data and conviction.
principles.quote: the establishment is often absolutely wrong. It's an act of courage to continue to say what you know to be right.

principles.text: Don't stoop to your critics' level; how you argue matters.
principles.quote: no matter how wrong your haters are, don't stoop to their level. When they go low, we go high.

principles.text: A breakthrough only has impact if you spread and communicate it effectively.
principles.quote: The breakthrough is only half of the work. The other half is spreading it to the rest of the world.
